req.title: Redirect-to accepts POST as well
req.statement: The system shall accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE on /redirect-to.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /redirect-to must accept POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, and TRACE methods. The source confirms the route decorator includes all these methods plus GET. Tests must verify: (1) each method returns a redirect status (302 by default), (2) the Location header is set exactly to the supplied URL, (3) custom status codes in the 3xx range are honoured, (4) status codes outside 3xx are ignored (defaults to 302), (5) unsupported methods (e.g. HEAD without explicit support beyond Flask defaults) behave correctly, and (6) boundary values around the 300/399 status code range are tested. The source reads 'url' from request.args (query string) for all methods, so all methods must pass url as a query parameter. Mutation-resilient assertions check exact status codes, exact Location header values, and boundary conditions at 299, 300, 399, 400.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_post_returns_302_with_location
preconditions: POST method is listed in route decorator
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_post_returns_302_with_location():
    r = client.post('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_post_returns_302_with_location()

preconditions: OPTIONS is not in the route's explicit method list
actions: Send OPTIONS request to /redirect-to?url=http://example.com (not in allowed methods list beyond Flask defaults)
expected: Response status code is 405 (Method Not Allowed) since OPTIONS is not explicitly listed
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_unsupported_method_returns_405():
    # OPTIONS is not in the explicit methods list for /redirect-to
    # Flask may handle OPTIONS automatically; use a truly unsupported custom method
    r = client.open('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com', method='CONNECT')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_redirect_to_unsupported_method_returns_405()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_methods_accept_and_return_3xx
preconditions: all five non-GET methods must be accepted
actions: Iterate POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE and assert each returns 302
expected: All five responses have Location header set to the target URL
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_methods_accept_and_return_3xx():
    target_url = 'http://example.com'
    methods = ['POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'PATCH', 'TRACE']
    for method in methods:
        r = client.open('/redirect-to?url=' + target_url, method=method)
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'{method} expected 302 got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == target_url, f'{method} bad Location: {r.headers.get("Location")}'

test_redirect_to_all_methods_accept_and_return_3xx()
